clue.text: Contribution from the same country

parts.note: DO is short for ditto, meaning the same as above
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: A gift that comes from one's own homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift or contribution made to a cause or charity.

clue.text: Murder mother to acquire estate

indicators.note: to acquire is to take in, so the murder phrase wraps round the mother word

parts.note: to do in is slang for to murder
MA is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone plots to kill their mother to inherit her property.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is an estate or territory owned or ruled by someone.

clue.text: Lack of employment is unacceptable for the Home Counties

parts.note: NON-U means not upper-class, socially unacceptable in old British usage
SE, the south-east of England, is where the Home Counties lie around London

explanation.surface: Unemployment is considered beneath the dignity of the comfortable counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in South-East England, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-use is the state of not being used or employed for anything.

clue.text: Reprimand for having broken the clock?

definitions.meaning: to scold someone is to give them a telling-off
a broken clock has had its ticking taken off, a whimsical reading of the phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: a clock that has stopped has lost its tick.
explanation.definitionFit: To tick someone off is to rebuke them; read literally it suggests a clock's tick removed.

clue.text: Past one's peak

parts.note: read literally, someone who has gone beyond a summit has crossed a hill; figuratively, someone too old to perform well

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone whose best years are behind them, especially through age.

clue.text: A way to confront the queen with a complaint

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
HM stands for Her Majesty, the queen

explanation.surface: Someone takes their grievance straight to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to confront' and 'with' simply join the pieces; the second 'a' supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint here means an ailment, and asthma is a chronic breathing disorder.

clue.text: Dues paid to get black gold underground

parts.note: subs are subscriptions, dues paid to a club
black gold is a nickname for crude oil

explanation.surface: Membership fees are invested in drilling for oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsoil is the layer of earth lying beneath the topsoil, below ground.

clue.text: Principal equipment needed to make hats

parts.note: a principal is the head of a school or organisation
gear is equipment or kit

explanation.surface: A milliner lists the main tools required for the trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Headgear is a collective word for hats and other coverings worn on the head.

clue.text: Andersen worked in Belgium and France

indicators.note: worked suggests the letters have been worked over into a new shape

explanation.surface: The fairy-tale writer Hans Christian Andersen did some work across two European countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ardennes is a forested upland region spanning Belgium, Luxembourg and France.

clue.text: Fellow airman escorted in shackles

parts.note: a fellow is a man
AC is aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank
led means guided or escorted

explanation.surface: A man and an RAF serviceman lead a prisoner in chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Manacled means bound with handcuffs or fetters, that is, in shackles.

clue.text: A table on ship

parts.note: a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A table is set out on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on or in a ship, aircraft or other vessel.

clue.text: Briefly, it's a popular drink of spirits

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a short is a small measure of spirits such as whisky

explanation.surface: Put simply, whisky is a well-liked tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: In short is a phrase meaning to sum up, in a few words.

clue.text: Oriental warlord carries model weapon

indicators.note: carries means holds within, so the warlord encloses the model

parts.note: a shogun was a hereditary military ruler of Japan
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A Japanese military leader carries a replica gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a smooth-bore firearm firing a spread of pellets.

clue.text: Arcane sign used by senior civil servants

parts.note: arcane means secret or mysterious
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Top bureaucrats use a mysterious symbol between themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the heads of government departments are Permanent Secretaries, senior civil servants.

clue.text: Europeans go, for unscheduled holiday

parts.note: the French are Europeans
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Some continental visitors depart for an unplanned break.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking French leave means absenting oneself without permission, an unofficial time off.

clue.text: He can't recall a cinema's programme

indicators.note: a programme arranges items in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has forgotten what is showing at the picture house.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesiac is a person suffering memory loss who cannot remember things.

clue.text: French priest comes round at four for healing

indicators.note: comes round means encircles, so the priest word wraps the other pieces

parts.note: cure is the French word for a parish priest
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A French cleric arrives at four o'clock to tend the sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Curative means able to cure disease, having healing power.

clue.text: Enumeration resulting in a cliff-hanger

indicators.note: resulting in signals that the letters turn out as a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A count produces a tense unresolved ending, as in a serial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff-hanger' looks like a suspenseful story ending; here it is literally one who hangs on cliffs.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber clinging to rock faces is jokingly a person hanging from a cliff.

clue.text: Filipino puts label on a piece of timber

parts.note: a tag is a label
a log is a piece of a felled tree

explanation.surface: A man from the Philippines labels a length of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagalog is a language of the Philippines, also a member of the people who speak it.

clue.text: Uniform for professional serviceman

definitions.meaning: uniform as an adjective means even and consistent, unvarying
a full-time soldier in the standing army, as opposed to a reservist

explanation.definitionFit: Regular means steady and unvarying, and a regular is a career soldier.

clue.text: Hardly the haunt for an imbibing poet!

definitions.text: Hardly the haunt for an imbibing poet!

parts.words: Hardly the haunt for an imbibing poet!
parts.note: split differently it is the name of a Restoration poet

explanation.surface: A tippling poet would never frequent a teetotal hangout.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a cryptic description of a dry den, an alcohol-free haunt; the exclamation mark flags the pun on the poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was a seventeenth-century English poet and Poet Laureate.

clue.text: A large number present remain loyal

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Many people attending stay faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere to a cause or person is to stick to it faithfully.

clue.text: Good news for Welshman and society girl

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh man's name
gel is the upper-class pronunciation of girl

explanation.surface: Glad tidings come for a Welsh fellow and a debutante.
explanation.walkthrough: GEL mimics how an upper-class English speaker pronounces girl, hence a society one.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel is an archaic term for the gospel, which literally means good news.

clue.text: Infuriated by explosion of grenade

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone is enraged by a bomb going off.
explanation.definitionFit: Angered means made angry, infuriated.

clue.text: In the Arctic I clearly saw many a one

definitions.text: In the Arctic I clearly saw many a one

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: A polar traveller reports seeing many of something frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: Icicles, hanging spikes of ice, are abundant in the frozen polar regions.

clue.text: Evict from the House of Hades

parts.note: Dis is another name for Hades, the god of the underworld
a lodge is a house, such as a gatekeeper's

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown out of the underworld's dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge is to force out from a position, as an evictor does.

clue.text: 150 grey-suited ministers

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: suited suggests the letters are fitted together in a new order

explanation.surface: A hundred and fifty government ministers in grey suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministers of religion collectively make up the clergy.

clue.text: Cause disaffection by serving English rum

parts.note: rum in British slang means odd or strange

explanation.surface: Pouring out English rum causes ill feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to alienate them, making them unfriendly.
